provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Welcome song
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the welcome song.
The pupils should be able to clap along with the beat.

Introduction:
We love to sing songs at school.
Today we will learn our special welcome song.

Content:
We will sing our welcome song together.
We will clap our hands to the beat.
The teacher will sing first.
Then the pupils will sing after the teacher.

Class activity:
We will form a circle and sing the welcome song.
We will clap our hands when we sing.
We will smile and wave to our friends.

Evaluation questions:
Can you sing the welcome song?
Show me how to clap to the beat.
What do we do when we sing?

Summary:
We learned our welcome song today.
We clapped our hands to the beat.

topics.title: Twinkle twinkle little star
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to point to stars.

Introduction:
We see stars at night.
Today we will learn a rhyme about stars.

Content:
The rhyme is Twinkle twinkle little star.
We will recite it with actions.
We will point up when we say star.
We will twinkle our fingers like stars.

Class activity:
We will look at pictures of stars.
We will point to the stars in the picture.
We will recite the rhyme together.

Evaluation questions:
What does the rhyme say about stars?
Show me how to twinkle your fingers.
Where do we point when we say star?

Summary:
We learned Twinkle twinkle little star.
We can point to stars in pictures.

topics.title: Rain rain go away
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to talk about rain and sun.

Introduction:
Rain comes from the sky.
Sometimes we want the sun to come out.

Content:
The rhyme is Rain rain go away.
We will recite it with actions.
We will make rain sounds with our hands.
We will open our arms wide for the sun.

Class activity:
We will pretend it is raining.
We will make rain sounds with our hands.
Then we will pretend the sun comes out.
We will open our arms wide.

Evaluation questions:
What does the rhyme say to the rain?
Show me how to make rain sounds.
What do we do when the sun comes out?

Summary:
We learned Rain rain go away.
We can talk about rain and sun.

topics.title: Pat a cake
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to play the clapping game.

Introduction:
We play games with our friends.
Today we will learn a clapping game.

Content:
The rhyme is Pat a cake.
We will recite it while clapping hands.
We will clap with a partner.
We will roll the pretend cake in our hands.

Class activity:
We will find a partner.
We will sit facing our partner.
We will clap hands while saying the rhyme.
We will take turns being the baker.

Evaluation questions:
What does the rhyme say about patting a cake?
Show me how to roll the cake.
How do we play the clapping game?

Summary:
We learned Pat a cake rhyme.
We can play the clapping game with friends.

topics.title: Johnny Johnny yes papa
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to play the sugar game.

Introduction:
Sometimes children eat sugar when they should not.
Today we will learn a rhyme about this.

Content:
The rhyme is Johnny Johnny yes papa.
We will recite it with actions.
We will point to our mouth when we eat sugar.
We will shake our head when we say no.

Class activity:
We will play the eat sugar or no sugar game.
The teacher will ask if we can eat sugar.
We will shake our head no.
We will pretend to brush our teeth.

Evaluation questions:
What does papa ask Johnny in the rhyme?
Show me how to say no.
What do we do after eating sugar?

Summary:
We learned Johnny Johnny yes papa.
We can play the sugar game.

topics.title: Baa baa black sheep
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to count bags of wool.

Introduction:
Sheep have wool on their bodies.
We can use wool to make clothes.

Content:
The rhyme is Baa baa black sheep.
We will recite it with actions.
We will pretend to be sheep and say baa.
We will count bags of wool one two three.

Class activity:
We will look at pictures of sheep.
We will count the bags of wool in the picture.
We will recite the rhyme together.
We will make sheep sounds.

Evaluation questions:
What does the black sheep have?
Show me how to count to three.
What sound does a sheep make?

Summary:
We learned Baa baa black sheep.
We can count bags of wool.

topics.title: Ding dong bell
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to act the cat and the mouse.

Introduction:
Cats like to chase mice.
Today we will learn a rhyme about them.

Content:
The rhyme is Ding dong bell.
We will recite it together.
We will pretend to ring a bell.
We will act the cat and the mouse.

Class activity:
We will pretend to be the cat.
We will pretend to be the mouse.
The cat will chase the mouse.
We will make meow and squeak sounds.

Evaluation questions:
What does the rhyme say about the cat?
Show me how to ring a bell.
What does the mouse do in the rhyme?

Summary:
We learned Ding dong bell.
We can act the cat and the mouse.

topics.title: Humpty Dumpty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme.
The pupils should be able to talk about being careful.

Introduction:
Sometimes we fall down.
We need to be careful not to get hurt.

Content:
The rhyme is Humpty Dumpty.
We will recite it with actions.
We will pretend to fall down.
We will put our hands together like a wall.

Class activity:
We will sit in a circle.
We will recite the rhyme together.
We will pretend to be Humpty Dumpty.
We will talk about being careful.

Evaluation questions:
What happened to Humpty Dumpty?
Show me how to be careful.
Why do we need to be careful?

Summary:
We learned Humpty Dumpty rhyme.
We can talk about being careful.

topics.title: Old MacDonald
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the song.
The pupils should be able to name farm animals.

Introduction:\ Farms have many animals.
Today we will learn about farm animals.

Content:
The song is Old MacDonald.
We will sing it with animal sounds.
We will name different farm animals.
We will make animal sounds like moo and oink.

Class activity:
We will look at pictures of farm animals.
We will name each animal.
We will make the animal sounds.
We will sing Old MacDonald together.

Evaluation questions:
What animals do we see on a farm?
Show me how a cow sounds.
What does Old MacDonald have on his farm?

Summary:
We learned Old MacDonald song.
We can name farm animals.

topics.title: Rhyme day revision
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing favourite rhymes.
The pupils should be able to clap as a class.

Introduction:
We have learned many rhymes this term.
Today we will sing our favourites.

Content:
We will pick our favourite rhymes.
We will sing them together.
We will clap our hands to the beat.
We will do the actions we learned.

Class activity:
We will vote for our favourite rhymes.
We will sing the rhymes that win.
We will clap and do actions.
We will have fun with rhymes.

Evaluation questions:
Which rhyme is your favourite?
Show me how to clap to the beat.
What action do we do for Twinkle twinkle?

Summary:
We revised our favourite rhymes.
We had fun singing and clapping.
